verses.text: Welcome the believer whose faith is still growing, but don’t turn different convictions into a debate.
One person trusts God and can eat anything; another whose faith is tender eats only vegetables.
The one who eats shouldn’t clown the one who doesn’t, and the one who doesn’t eat shouldn’t judge the one who does. God has welcomed them both.
Who are you to judge somebody else’s servant? Their own master decides whether they stand or fall. And they will stand, because the Lord has power to hold them up.
One person treats a certain day as special; someone else treats every day the same. Each person should be settled in their own mind.
The person who observes a day does it for the Lord. The one who doesn’t, also does it for the Lord. The one who eats gives thanks to God; the one who skips it gives thanks too.
None of us lives just for ourselves, and none of us dies just for ourselves.
If we live, we live for the Lord; if we die, we die for the Lord. Alive or dead, we belong to the Lord.
That’s why Christ died, came back to life, and lives again: so he could be Lord of both the dead and the living.
So why judge your brother or sister? And why look down on them? We’re all going to stand before Christ’s judgment seat.
Scripture says, “‘As surely as I live,’ says the Lord, ‘every knee will bow to me, and every tongue will praise God.’”
So each of us will answer to God for ourselves.
Let’s stop judging each other. Instead, decide not to put a stumbling block—or a trap—in another believer’s way.
I’m convinced in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean by itself. But if someone considers something unclean, then for them it is unclean.
If your food hurts your brother or sister, you’re no longer walking in love. Don’t wreck someone Christ died for over what you eat.
Don’t let what you consider good become something people drag through the mud.
God’s Kingdom isn’t about what you eat or drink. It’s about righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.
Whoever serves Christ this way is pleasing to God and respected by people.
So let’s chase what brings peace and helps each other grow stronger.
Don’t tear down God’s work over food. Everything is clean, but it’s wrong to eat in a way that trips someone up.
It’s better to skip meat, wine, or anything else if it makes your brother or sister stumble, offended, or weak.
Keep your faith about these things between you and God. Happy is the person who doesn’t condemn themselves over what they believe is right.
But if someone has doubts and still eats, they’re condemned, because they aren’t acting from faith. Anything that doesn’t come from faith is sin.
Now to the One who can make you stand strong in line with the Good News I preach and the message about Jesus Christ,
the mystery kept under wraps for ages, but now brought to light and made known through the prophetic Scriptures by the command of the eternal God, so every nation may come to faith and obedience—
to the only wise God, through Jesus Christ, be glory forever! Amen. 🙌
